record.paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
record.original_question: In string theories with higher-order corrections relevant to ekpyrotic or cyclic cosmology, does the compactified Milne mod Z2 × R3 space that models the reversal phase emerge asymptotically as a stable attractor when the higher-order terms are asymptotically subdominant and the matter content is a fluid with a general equation of state?

evidence.quote: What remains is an interesting issue (that can be fully addressed with the asymptotic methods used in [47]) as follows: Find whether the ‘compactiﬁed Milne mod Z2 × R3 space’ monitoring the reversal phase in the ekpyrotic and cyclic scenarios, also emerges asymptotically as a stable attractor in the dynamics of higher-order gravity when the matter content is a ﬂuid with a general equation of state.

4.5 Ekpyrosis and the Milne state with asymptotically subdominant higher-order terms
This project aims to examine the global asymptotic stability of the Milne state in string theories with higher-order corrections in an eﬀort to decide as to whether or not this state is a viable representative of the passage through the singularity in models with an ekpyrotic or cyclic phase.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider higher-order (curvature-corrected) gravitational theories in four spacetime dimensions whose action consists of the Einstein–Hilbert term together with higher-order curvature invariants (for example, terms quadratic or of higher order in the Riemann/Ricci tensors and the Ricci scalar), coupled to a perfect-fluid matter source with a general barotropic equation of state p = wρ, w ∈ ℝ. Assume that the higher-order curvature contributions are asymptotically subdominant relative to the Einstein–Hilbert term in the regime under study.

Within this class of theories, consider the model spacetime "compactified Milne mod ℤ₂ × ℝ³", i.e. the product of three-dimensional flat Euclidean space ℝ³ with the quotient of two-dimensional Milne space (the Lorentzian cone ds² = −dt² + t² dy², t > 0) by a ℤ₂ identification together with a compactification of the y-direction; this geometry is the candidate description of the reversal/bounce phase in ekpyrotic and cyclic cosmological scenarios.

Question: Determine whether the compactified Milne mod ℤ₂ × ℝ³ spacetime emerges as a global asymptotic attractor of the cosmological dynamical system associated with such higher-order gravity theories sourced by a fluid with a general equation of state. That is, prove or disprove that, for generic initial data within an open set of cosmological solutions and for all admissible values of w, the trajectories of the field equations converge asymptotically to this Milne-type state, and characterize the range of w (if any) for which this stability holds.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a published proof or disproof establishing the compactified Milne mod ℤ₂ × ℝ³ state as a global asymptotic attractor of higher-order gravity dynamics with a general-equation-of-state fluid. Related works treat stability of ekpyrotic contracting phases and modified-gravity cyclic models, but the specific global asymptotic stability question for the Milne reversal state with subdominant higher-order corrections appears not to be settled in the literature available.

status_evidence.title: Inflation vs. Ekpyrosis — Comparing stability in general non-minimal theory
status_evidence.snippet: Studies relative stability of ekpyrotic and inflationary phases in non-minimal/higher-order frames, but does not establish the Milne state as a global attractor.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses ekpyrotic stability in higher-order/non-minimal gravity but does not resolve the specific Milne attractor question.

status_evidence.title: Cyclic, ekpyrotic and little rip universe in modified gravity
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs cyclic and ekpyrotic cosmologies in modified gravity without proving global asymptotic stability of the compactified Milne reversal state.
status_evidence.claim: Modified-gravity ekpyrotic/cyclic models exist but the Milne state's global attractor status remains unverified.

status_evidence.title: No-go theorems for ekpyrosis from ten-dimensional supergravity
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes obstructions to ekpyrosis in 10D supergravity, indirectly indicating the dynamical question is unresolved in higher-order frameworks.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates ongoing investigation rather than resolution of ekpyrotic attractor questions.
